CPH / state government — Armazém 10 of the Port of Belém converted into a COP30 waterway terminal, expecting >190,000 passengers during the conference

regulator: ARTRAN/PA (state waterway transport regulation; successor to ARCON-PA); CPH — Companhia de Portos e Hidrovias do Estado do Pará (state terminal owner/operator); Prefeitura de Belém (municipal island lines incl. Geladão Fluvial); Capitania dos Portos da Amazônia Oriental / Brazilian Navy (vessel certification); ANTAQ (federal waterway authority)
annual_basis_note: DISPLAY-ONLY market: no promotion of these figures into economics until the Amazon lane gets its own evidence pass. The only official annual series found is ARTRAN's 553,823 pax (2024) for the STATE intermunicipal system — it excludes Belém's municipal island lines (Combu, Cotijuba, Mosqueiro) and informal crossings, so true Belém-basin waterborne volume is materially higher. Terminal-level official annual counts not yet published for the new (Oct–Nov 2025) terminals.
gaps: No official per-terminal annual passenger series for Terminal Hidroviário de Belém, Tamandaré or Ruy Barata; the new terminals opened Oct–Nov 2025 so first full-year data will only exist after 2026.
Municipal (intra-Belém) island-line ridership (Combu, Cotijuba geladão, Mosqueiro) not published as a series — only fares, capacities (208–220 pax vessels) and one-off surge reports.
Plano Mestre 456k Porto de Belém interior-navigation pax figure: measurement year not confirmed (report is pre-2020) — verify before use.
July-2026 300k figure is a government projection for one month, not an outturn.
COP30 aquaviário terminal (Armazém 10) final ridership outturn not yet published (190k was the pre-conference expectation).
Combu annual visitor count not found from an official source (only qualitative density: hourly boats, 40+ restaurants).
Coordinates unresolved for Terminal Hidroviário da Tamandaré and Trapiche Poeta Antônio Tavernard (Mosqueiro) — candidate OSM piers noted in boarding-points.json, null until confirmed.
